clue.text: Two fellows after fruit hard to resist

indicators.note: after says the fellows come behind the fruit and hard to

parts.note: a fig is a fruit
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
F is short for fellow, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: Someone tries to fend off a hard fruit being pressed on them by two men.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'after' makes the two fellows come last, though the clue names them first.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist an attacker or an illness is to repel or ward it off.

clue.text: Join fleet on bearing to the north

parts.note: fleet means quick or swift

indicators.note: in a down clue going to the north means the letters are read upwards, back to front

parts.note: NE, north-east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A navy fleet links up while sailing on a northerly course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' turns NE into EN, since a down answer reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to fasten two things is to attach or join them.

clue.text: Care given preparing beef

indicators.note: preparing suggests ingredients being worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Care is taken over cooking a joint of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like the meat being prepared; it is slang for a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: a beef is a complaint or gripe.

clue.text: Splashed custard on suit in tragedy

indicators.note: splashed suggests the letters scattered about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spills custard on their suit during a tragic moment.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Shakespeare's bloodiest early play is a Roman revenge tragedy.

clue.text: The creeps pinching European goods

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight, so one piece is gripped inside the other

parts.note: having the creeps means feeling fear, a fright

explanation.surface: Sinister people stealing goods from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The creeps' reads as shady people, but it means a feeling of fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: freight is cargo, goods carried by ship, lorry or plane.

clue.text: Very brief yen to stop affair

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: a fling is a brief love affair
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A quick longing puts an end to a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' reads as a longing but is the currency abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a flying visit is a hurried, very short one.

clue.text: Watch orator, perhaps, that's rich

parts.note: to watch is to look
an orator is an example of one who is talking, giving a speech

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a speaker and remarks on how wealthy he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's rich' looks like praise of wealth; it is the sarcastic retort to a hypocrite.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idiomatic retorts accusing someone of hypocrisy in what they just said.

clue.text: People using coins and notes endlessly

parts.note: in can mean using, as in written in ink

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: coins and notes together are cash

explanation.surface: Someone pays with coins and an endless stream of banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the H from CASH.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were a South American people who built an empire in the Andes.

clue.text: With GPS primarily nowadays, cop tracks devices

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: AD, anno domini, denotes the present era
to cop is to get or catch
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of tracks

explanation.surface: Police now follow suspects with satellite navigation and other gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cop' looks like a police officer but is the verb meaning get.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadgetry is a collective term for gadgets, mechanical or electronic devices.

clue.text: American fool with bottom above head gets exhausted

indicators.note: in a down answer the bottom letter is shifted to sit above the top one

parts.note: to dupe is to fool, and a dupe is a fool

explanation.surface: An American idiot stands on his head and wears himself out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with bottom above head' moves the final E of DUPE to its top, giving EDUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be used up is to be spent, worn out or exhausted.

clue.text: Son isn't paragon of virtue

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A parent remarks that their son is no model of good behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint is a person of exceptional goodness, the very model of virtue.

clue.text: Comfortably settled, three bridge players yield to contract

parts.note: E, N and S are three of the four bridge seats: East, North, South

indicators.note: to contract means to shorten, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: to yield is to concede

explanation.surface: Three bridge players, comfortably seated, give way on the contract they bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' suggests a bridge bid; it means shorten, dropping the last E of CONCEDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be ensconced is to be snugly established in a place.

clue.text: Imagined gnarled vine's old

indicators.note: gnarled means twisted and knotted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: old means aged

explanation.surface: Someone pictures an ancient, twisted grapevine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnarled' rearranges VINES into ENVIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to envisage something is to picture or imagine it.

clue.text: Pronounced part of body is unwanted

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the word is given by how it sounds

parts.note: the waist is the part of the body between ribs and hips

explanation.surface: A prominent bit of someone's physique is undesirable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' looks like 'prominent'; it signals that the body part is heard, not spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective waste describes material discarded as no longer wanted.

clue.text: Somewhat drunk, no trouble to relax

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Being a little tipsy is an easy way to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: Untying a knot loosens it, so the word means to slacken or relax.

clue.text: Extremely pitiful stranger is drudge

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: stranger means odder, more peculiar

explanation.surface: A rather sad outsider ends up doing menial work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'pitiful' but takes its outer letters, P and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a plodder works slowly and laboriously at dull tasks, like a drudge.

clue.text: Passed to acquire Cockney's item, about one grand

indicators.note: to acquire means to take in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: passed away means died

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: an item is a thing, which in Cockney speech becomes fing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dead man's estate includes a Cockney's possession worth around a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney drops TH for F, so 'thing' is FING; 'about' reverses it to GNIF. 'grand' looks like a thousand pounds but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: grand and dignified both describe an imposing, stately bearing.

clue.text: Jolly dad worried with spaniel scratching two areas

indicators.note: worried means harried and shaken about, so the letters are rearranged
scratching means striking out, so these letters are removed from the pool

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, so two of them give AA

explanation.surface: A cheerful father frets about his spaniel scratching two patches of skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching' reads as a dog's itch but strikes out two As (areas) from the pool that 'worried' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal exclamations of approval: something jolly good is excellent.

clue.text: French entertainer's mimic that is replacing another, initially

indicators.note: replacing means one piece takes the place of another inside the word

parts.note: a parrot mimics speech, and to parrot is to mimic

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A French performer's impressionist stands in for a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' puts IE in place of the A ('another, initially') in PARROT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the sad-faced clown, a stock figure of French pantomime.

clue.text: Announcements of town events so regularly ignored

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter is skipped, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: News of local happenings is routinely overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Posts on the social platform once called Twitter are short public announcements.

clue.text: Feel free to label start of eighties as second childhood

parts.note: do, as in do come in, invites someone to feel free
a tag is a label

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: An invitation to call someone in their eighties childish.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: old age bringing feebleness of mind is called a second childhood.

clue.text: Maybe cup final referee

definitions.meaning: a cup final is an example of a match that settles a contest
a referee is one who settles disputes

explanation.surface: Perhaps the official in charge of a cup final.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a deciding match and an arbiter settle the outcome of something.

clue.text: Orders of barrows with hundred-fold increase

indicators.note: multiplying the Roman five by a hundred gives the Roman five hundred, so one numeral is swapped for another

parts.note: a barrow is an ancient burial mound, a grave

explanation.surface: Classes of wheelbarrows multiplied a hundred times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrows' suggests wheelbarrows; they are burial mounds. V (5) times 100 is D (500).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: grades and orders are both ranks or classes in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Petite Spaniard's the female on-trend

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
in means fashionable, on-trend

explanation.surface: A small, fashionable Spanish woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes someone small and delicate, like an elf.

clue.text: Voguish tips from family to nurse tot

indicators.note: to nurse means to hold close, so one piece goes inside the other
tips are the ends, so the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: Fashionable advice from relatives on caring for a toddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a toddler, but is the verb meaning add.
explanation.definitionFit: Faddy means following fads, short-lived fashions, so it is near to voguish.

clue.text: Six Creole cooks for hotel, perhaps

indicators.note: cooks means prepares or doctors, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Six Creole chefs work for a hotel kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooks' reads as chefs but is a verb signalling rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Excelsior is a common name for grand hotels.

clue.text: Hard working cadet died in action

indicators.note: in action means set in motion, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A diligent military trainee was killed in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dedicated person is committed and diligent.

clue.text: Work in Greek island secured by one youth

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: secured by means held fast by, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A job on a Greek island taken by a young man.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem of the Trojan War is a work written in Greek.

clue.text: In the case of drought, grain is most parched

indicators.note: in places the grain inside the other letters
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: rye is a grain, and 's is short for is, giving rye's

explanation.surface: During a drought, cereal crops are at their driest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the case of drought' gives D and T, around RYE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of dry, meaning having the least moisture.

clue.text: Teams requested to stock kit (small)

indicators.note: to stock means to hold within, so the kit goes inside

parts.note: bade is a past tense of bid, to request or command
rig means kit or equipment

explanation.surface: Groups are asked to carry kit in small sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigades are organised groups or teams, such as fire brigades.
